Filtering with a Conditional where

GET /tickets?status=open — building Prisma's where clause only when a filter was actually given.

listTicketsQuerySchema (Figure 3.6, earlier topic) already validates and defaults every option a GET /tickets request can carry — status, sortBy, order, page, pageSize — before the controller ever sees them. ticket.service.js is where those options actually turn into a Prisma query:

// Figure 3.13: filtering, sorting, and paginating in one query (src/services/ticket.service.js)
export const getAllTickets = async ({ status, sortBy, order, page, pageSize }) => {
  const where = status ? { status } : undefined;

  const [tickets, total] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.ticket.findMany({
      where,
      orderBy: { [sortBy]: order },
      skip: (page - 1) * pageSize,
      take: pageSize,
      include: { customer: userSummary, assignedAgent: userSummary },
    }),
    prisma.ticket.count({ where }),
  ]);

  return { tickets, total };
};

status is optional in the schema — a bare GET /tickets has no filter at all — so where is built conditionally: { status } when one was given, or undefined when it wasn't. Prisma treats an undefined where as "no filter," which is exactly the behavior a missing query param should have. Passing that same where to both findMany and count (next slide's Promise.all covers why they run together) matters just as much: the count has to reflect the same filtered set the list itself does, or total would describe a different set of tickets than what actually came back.
